propositions: When re-reviewing a plan with a prior BLOCK verdict, a deterministic pre-check compares cited evidence anchors from blocking findings against the current plan text to detect if the material cited in the block has not been addressed.

If all matched evidence anchors remain verbatim unchanged and the description component fingerprint is identical, a warn-only alert is logged before review execution, naming the persisting blocking findings and their criteria.
The pre-check never hard-blocks or declines; it logs a warning and allows the review to run, honoring the escape-hatch requirement for the ~8% of BLOCK→PASS verdict flips with no material change.

Findings with unmatchable anchors (paraphrased or structural) do not trigger the warning independently; the warning fires only when at least one anchor matched old text and all matched anchors are untouched.
The warning presence/absence is recorded in sidecar metrics as precheck.cited_anchor_warning on every plan review to enable offline measurement of hit rate and predictive value.
